Sam: Heads-up — found a repro for a nasty race with the Python SDK AsyncClient + auth refresh. After a long-lived process under load, requests start failing with "Event loop is closed".
Morgan: Can you paste the smallest repro or snippet?
Sam: Sure, here's the minimal pattern that hits it pretty reliably in our sample app:
```py
from httpx import AsyncClient

async def ping():
    client = AsyncClient(..., auth=AuthRefresh())
    await client.get("/ping")

# AuthRefresh internally spins a background refresh that does:
# asyncio.run(self._do_refresh()) inside a ThreadPoolExecutor task
```
Sam: My suspicion is the refresh path calls `asyncio.run()` from a worker thread which creates and then closes an event loop; under certain scheduling that seems to leak into the main loop and subsequent awaits start raising "Event loop is closed". Happens intermittently, more under concurrency.
Ivy: Oof. Which SDK version?
Sam: 0.12.3-beta (the quickstart sample uses it).
Alex: Is this related to the earlier sync-refresh-on-thread bug we patched? That used `get_event_loop()` incorrectly.
Sam: Slightly different — the problematic code does `asyncio.run()` (creates a brand new loop and closes it) rather than reusing the parent loop. If the ThreadPool thread briefly becomes the context for other asyncio ops, closing that loop seems to race.
Morgan: Quick try: can you replace `asyncio.run` with an explicit `loop = asyncio.new_event_loop(); asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)` pattern and avoid closing it immediately? Or better: make the refresh callback accept an explicit loop reference so it runs on the main loop with `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`.
Ivy: Also a DX/typing note: AuthRefresh isn't typed as accepting sync vs async callers — we should make the contract explicit and provide a sync shim. Lots of users assume they can call refresh from sync threads.
Alex: Filing a bug and a patch suggestion — RN-3345. I'll draft a PR that: 1) removes `asyncio.run` from background threads, 2) uses `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe` when invoked from non-loop threads, 3) adds unit + stress test.
Sam: Workaround for now: call `await client.aclose()` on graceful shutdown and pin to 0.12.2 if you hit this in production. Also avoid creating refresh tasks via executor until we push a patch.
Morgan: Can you attach a tiny repro script and I'll run it under our CI stress harness? If it reproduces we can gate the patch on that test.
Sam: Will attach in a minute. Repro is ~40 lines and reproduces in 10-30s under 50 concurrent workers.
ci-bot: Created issue repo:redwood/python-sdk#3345 (RN-3345) and linked draft PR redwood/python-sdk#3346-draft
Alex: Nice. Also can we add a small note in quickstart about async vs sync auth patterns so customers don't hit this by accident?
Ivy: Yes — UX asks: add a short section showing proper async AuthRefresh implementation and recommend `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe` for background threads.
Sam: Thanks everyone, I'll post the repro + tentative fix in the issue. :thumbsup:
